title: Progressive rendering and tooltip fusion for dense time-series lanes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Improve perceived performance and accessibility of our multi-series time-series components by implementing a progressive paint strategy, lane compression for high-density data, and a unified 'tooltip fusion' pattern that consolidates overlapping tooltips. This ticket covers visual tokens, interaction states, keyboard scrubbing, and performance measurement hooks for the engineering team.
background: Current time-series charts struggle on low-memory devices and when rendering dozens of short, dense series. Tooltips for overlapping points create noise and are awkward for keyboard users. Our existing approach renders all series synchronously and shows separate tooltips per series which increases DOM updates and reduces clarity for users comparing series.
problem_statement: We need a single, predictable pattern that: 1) reduces initial paint cost for high-series charts, 2) keeps interaction accessible (focus, keyboard scrubbing, aria-live), and 3) surfaces cross-series comparisons without overwhelming the user with multiple floating tooltips.
proposed_solution: 1) Progressive paint pipeline: render axis, grid, and top N series synchronously (N configurable by profile), hydrate remaining series in idle callbacks; 2) Lane compression: when >M series, collapse visual representation into compact lanes with aggregated sparkline summaries and per-lane expand on hover/focus; 3) Tooltip fusion: a single anchor tooltip that aggregates nearest-point values from visible series and supports keyboard focus + aria-live announcements; 4) Expose tokens for compressed lane height, focus outline, tooltip spacing in our design tokens so engineering can theme consistently.
tradeoffs:
- Progressive paint increases initial visual stability but may delay detail for lower-priority series.
- Lane compression reduces information density which may obscure outliers until expanded.
- Tooltip fusion simplifies surface area but requires robust UX to avoid hiding series-level nuance.
acceptance_criteria: Axis and grid paint within 120ms on target low-end device profile (measured via Lighthouse emulation)
Top N series render synchronously; remaining series complete within 500ms during idle time on typical desktop
When >16 series, chart defaults to compressed-lane view and keyboard users can tab through lanes to expand a lane
Single fused tooltip displays aggregated values for visible series and is read by screen readers via aria-live when keyboard-scrub position changes
Design token entries added: token.chart.compressedLaneHeight, token.chart.tooltipGap, token.chart.focusRingWidth
Unit/regression tests covering tooltip fusion logic and lane compression toggles
Documentation and usage example added to component library with knobs for N and M thresholds
design_notes:
- Visual tokens: propose compressedLaneHeight = 20px, expandedLaneHeight = 72px, laneGap = 8px.
- Focus states use accessible 3:1 contrast ring per accessible colors guide; outline thickness tokenized for platform parity.
- Tooltip fusion layout: header shows timestamp, body lists series color swatch + label + value, footer shows comparison delta when applicable.
- Motion: use a cross-fade when hydrating additional series to avoid layout shift.
- Provide an 'always-show-series' override prop for power users.

Implement lane-compression render mode and compressed->expanded transition API
Implement fused-tooltip component with keyboard and screen-reader hooks
Add design tokens to theme and update docs
Add telemetry hooks: initial-paint, hydration-complete, tooltip-open, lane-expand for perf dashboards
Write unit and integration tests; add visual tests for compressed and expanded states
qa_checks: Simulate 32-series dataset on mobile emulation and record first contentful paint
Keyboard-only navigation: Tab to chart, use arrow keys to scrub and confirm aria-live announcements
Screen reader: NVDA/VoiceOver readback for tooltip content when scrubbing
Visual regression: compressed lanes, expanded lane overlay, tooltip fusion snapshot
Memory regression: monitor heap delta during a long scroll with many charts
ux_research: Run moderated test with 6 designers/engineers comparing existing tooltip-per-series vs fused-tooltip for cross-series comparison tasks. Measure time-to-insight and subjective clarity. Capture notes on toggle discoverability for compressed lanes.
